newsitem.title: USA: Jefferson Cty, Ala., plans $320 mln March issue.
newsitem.headline: Jefferson Cty, Ala., plans $320 mln March issue.

text.p: Alabama's Jefferson County plans a $320 million water revenue bond issue on March 4, county finance director Steve Saylor said Friday.
Raymond James & Associates Inc is senior manager for the neogitated deal, Saylor said.

The new money issue follows last week's $259 million revenue warrant refinancing issue by the county, which consolidated all the water system's outstanding debt and relieved it of restrictive debt covenenants, Saylor said.
"Combined, it's the largest issue in the state of Alabama," Saylor said.

The debt issues will finance water system upgrades to bring the county in compliance with a federal consent decree. In 1995, the federal government charged the county with violating the Clean Water Act by allowing untreated wastewater to be discharged into the Cahaba and Black Warrier rivers.

The county also plans a $50 million general obligation warrant issue later in the spring to complete asbestos removal at its main courthouse and finance upgrades to bring the building into compliance with the Americans With Disabilities Act, Saylor said.
By comparison with the water deal, "That one will be pretty tame," Saylor said.

The warrant issue also will be a negotiated deal but the underwriting team has not yet been chosen. Saylor said there was no referendum on the issue because none is required in Alabama for general obligation warrant issues.
